controller_actions.task: Rewrite module.py implementing solve(data) per the user contract. Process data['ops'] in order without mutating input. Per operation, check in this exact order: (1) kind in credit/debit/hold/release else ValueError; (2) for credit/debit/hold, amount must be int (not bool) and >=1 else ValueError; (3) hold: id must not be an active hold; release: id must be an active hold, else ValueError (release ignores amount); (4) for debit and hold, amount must not exceed available (balance - held) else ValueError. credit adds to balance; debit subtracts; hold records holds[id]=amount; release removes it. Return {'balance':int,'held':int,'available':int} where held is sum of active holds and available=balance-held. Empty ops returns zeros. Standard library only, no I/O.

Write test_cases.json: a JSON list of at least 8 distinct cases, each {"name":..., "input":{"ops":[...]}, and exactly one of "output":{"balance":int,"held":int,"available":int} or "error":"ValueError"}. Follow the user contract exactly: ops applied in order; kinds credit/debit/hold/release; amount must be int>=1 (bool rejected) for credit/debit/hold; hold id must not be active, release id must be active (release ignores amount); debit/hold amount must not exceed available=balance-held. Cover: empty ops -> zeros; credit then debit; hold reducing available; release restoring availability and ignoring amount; unknown kind error; bool amount error; zero/negative amount error; duplicate hold id error; release unknown id error; debit exceeding available due to hold error; hold exceeding available error; reuse of id after release succeeds; check ordering (e.g. invalid amount on hold with duplicate id still ValueError).
